chablis/chardonnay.match: Chablis AOC identifies the Chardonnay appellation represented here; the grape may not be printed prominently.
chablis/chardonnay.limit: Petit Chablis, Premier Cru and Grand Cru are separate appellation levels. Chablis alone does not promise steel-only ageing, a particular oak note or the atlas's exact scores.
chablis/chardonnay.check: Confirm Chablis AOC, then check the producer's cuvée and oak/fermentation notes if you want the young, steel-led reference.

bordeaux/cabernet-sauvignon.example: Bordeaux AOC · producer confirms Cabernet Sauvignon-led red blend
bordeaux/cabernet-sauvignon.match: The producer's blend information, rather than 'Bordeaux' on its own, connects a bottle to this Cabernet-led dry-red reference.
bordeaux/cabernet-sauvignon.limit: Bordeaux includes white and red wines and many red blends. The appellation does not certify Cabernet dominance, a fixed blend, oak recipe or flavour score.
bordeaux/cabernet-sauvignon.check: Ask the shop or restaurant for the producer and cuvée, then check the technical sheet or back label for grape composition and vintage.

bordeaux/merlot.example: Bordeaux AOC · producer confirms Merlot-led red blend
bordeaux/merlot.match: The producer's blend information connects this bottle to the Merlot-led reference. A place name by itself does not identify the leading grape.
bordeaux/merlot.limit: Merlot-led does not mean 100% Merlot. Bordeaux AOC alone does not establish a blend percentage, oak regime or a softer wine in every vintage.
bordeaux/merlot.check: Confirm the cuvée's actual grape composition with the producer or seller; check vintage and oak details separately.

valpolicella/corvina.match: This names the Valpolicella Classico expression modeled as a fresh-grape, Corvina-led regional blend.
valpolicella/corvina.limit: Corvina-led is an atlas reference, not a promise that the bottle is a single-variety wine. Ripasso, Amarone and sweet Recioto are different named expressions.
valpolicella/corvina.check: Read the full designation; choose Valpolicella Classico DOC without Ripasso for this lighter comparison. Confirm producer, vintage and oak choices.

amarone/corvina.match: Amarone names the dry, grape-drying (appassimento) red expression represented here; the label need not say Corvina.
amarone/corvina.limit: Dried-grape aromas are not a sugar reading. Amarone is distinct from sweet Recioto; the label does not fix blend, oak, alcohol warmth or vintage character.
amarone/corvina.check: Confirm the full Amarone designation, not Valpolicella or Ripasso. Check producer information for sweetness and maturation if comparing a specific bottle.

prosecco-doc/glera.match: Prosecco DOC identifies the designation; Spumante identifies sparkling wine. Extra Dry is a regulated sweetness term, with more residual sugar than Brut.
prosecco-doc/glera.limit: 'Extra Dry' does not mean bone-dry. Prosecco DOC also spans other sweetness levels and Frizzante; the atlas's dry-to-off-dry tank-method reference is not every bottle.
prosecco-doc/glera.check: Look for DOC, Spumante and the sweetness wording. Choose Extra Dry for an off-dry leaning comparison or check Brut for a drier bottle; consult the producer for method and exact sugar.

jerez-fino/palomino.match: Fino is the dry, pale Sherry style aged under a film of flor yeast represented here; Palomino may not be the large front-label word.
jerez-fino/palomino.limit: Sherry is not one sweetness or one ageing style. Fino does not stand in for Oloroso, Cream or sweet Pedro Ximénez.
jerez-fino/palomino.check: Confirm Fino and the Sherry designation; do not substitute a sweet or oxidative style for a Fino tasting contrast.

jerez-oloroso/palomino.match: A dry Oloroso identifies the oxidative-aged Palomino Sherry reference here.
jerez-oloroso/palomino.limit: Oloroso-derived sweet blends and Cream are not this dry reference. Dark colour and nutty aromas alone do not prove sugar content.
jerez-oloroso/palomino.check: Ask whether the listed Oloroso is dry/seco, especially on a short restaurant list; check the producer's style information.

jerez-px/pedro-ximenez.match: This names the sweet, raisined-grape Pedro Ximénez Sherry expression represented here.
jerez-px/pedro-ximenez.limit: PX is not a synonym for all Sherry, nor does it describe the dry Palomino Fino or Oloroso profiles.
jerez-px/pedro-ximenez.check: Confirm the full style and designation; if the menu only says 'Sherry', ask which style and whether it is sweet.

niagara-icewine/vidal-blanc.example: VQA Niagara Peninsula Icewine · Vidal Blanc
niagara-icewine/vidal-blanc.match: VQA Niagara Peninsula identifies the Ontario origin and Icewine category; Vidal Blanc identifies the grape for this sweet reference.
niagara-icewine/vidal-blanc.limit: Niagara alone does not mean Icewine. Late Harvest is a different category; Icewine alone does not choose a grape or promise the atlas's notes.
niagara-icewine/vidal-blanc.check: Confirm VQA, Niagara Peninsula and Icewine. Check grape/producer information for Vidal; if the grape is absent, do not assume it.

niagara-icewine/riesling.match: VQA Niagara Peninsula and Icewine establish the origin and naturally frozen-grape category; Riesling selects this represented expression.
niagara-icewine/riesling.limit: The appellation and Icewine term do not identify the grape without further information or fix acidity, sweetness or aroma scores for a particular bottle.
niagara-icewine/riesling.check: Confirm the Icewine wording and region, then the grape on the label or producer sheet. Late Harvest and other grapes are different selections.

niagara-icewine/cabernet-franc.example: VQA Niagara Peninsula Icewine · Cabernet Franc
niagara-icewine/cabernet-franc.match: The VQA origin and Icewine term identify the Ontario category; Cabernet Franc selects the represented red-grape Icewine.
niagara-icewine/cabernet-franc.limit: Icewine does not imply white grapes; a red-grape example can differ in colour and notes. The category does not set the atlas's exact scores.
niagara-icewine/cabernet-franc.check: Confirm the Icewine wording, Niagara Peninsula origin and Cabernet Franc on the label or producer information.
